## Problem

The distill cache salt hashed the agent, model and effort alongside the prompt, reconcile prompt and threshold. The facts are the product, not the model that produced them, so keying on the model meant the setup backfill (a resolved agent, effort low) and the session-end hook (auto, no effort) never shared a cache entry. Each re-spent on every session the other had already distilled.

On a real 289-session brain: a bare `entire brain distill --dry-run` reported **0 cached**, while `--agent codex --effort low` reported 72 of the same sessions. No facts had landed from the hook for 16 days.

## Change

- `distillCacheSalt` now covers only what the extractor was asked (prompt with taxonomy, reconcile prompt, confidence threshold) and the preprocessing version.
- Entries older binaries wrote under the agent-bearing formula are grandfathered against an enumerated set of known producer salts (the current run's own, plus codex and claude-code with and without effort low and a pinned model, in both preprocessing versions) and rewritten under the new salt on first sight. The hook migrates what the backfill wrote and vice versa; nobody has to repeat the writer's flags.
- The checkpoint fast path, the file-era-to-checkpoint content migration and the per-chunk reuse cache get the same grandfathering.
- The three salt derivations (current, legacy, legacy agent-bearing) share one prompt/threshold resolution.

## Tests

- `TestDistillCacheSaltIgnoresAgentModelEffort`: salt equality across agent, model, effort and agent command; prompt, reconcile, threshold and preprocessing version still invalidate.
- `TestDistillGrandfathersAgentSaltedCacheEntries`: seeded legacy entries cost zero agent calls on the backfill run, are rewritten under the new salt, cost zero calls on the hook's configuration, migrate under the hook's configuration too, and changed content still re-distills.
- `TestLegacyAgentDistillCacheSaltsEnumerateKnownProducers`, `TestDistillGrandfathersAgentSaltedCheckpointEntries` (identity entries and file-era content entries on a checkpoint-backed brain), `TestDistillChunkDoneUnderLegacySalt`.
- `TestDistillDryRunPredictsCacheAccurately` inverted: a different model now predicts all cached; a changed threshold predicts re-distill.
- `go test ./internal/cli/` passes.

## Verified on a real brain

Dry run with this build after one backfill pass: 147 cached under the default agent and under `--agent codex --effort low` alike. The pre-fix binary reports 0 cached for the same store under its default agent.

==== ISSUE COMMENTS ====
6386729205	suhaanthayyil
Independent adversarial review (second pass, separate from the agent review that passed). **The thesis is right and the implementation is well guarded** — 18 of 20 weakenings went red, including every arm of the producer enumeration, both grandfathering call sites, and the content binding. I could not break the branch partitioning: branch is in the cache key *and* in both fingerprint forms, and it takes two simultaneous weakenings to lose it. Duplicate session ids are handled: grandfathering is reached only after a hit on the already-discriminated key.

Two things to fix before this lands.

---

### 1. A zero-record extraction is now permanently sticky — `distill_cmd.go:1483`

A chunk whose agent call **succeeds but yields no usable records** takes the `len(records) == 0 → continue` path at `distill_cmd.go:1458` without setting `sessionFailed`. The session is then cached as distilled (`:1483`) with an empty facts file.

Before this PR that was self-healing by accident: the next run under a different agent/model/effort produced a different salt, so the fingerprint did not match and the session was re-distilled. After this PR the salt is producer-independent by design, so `prev == ps.fingerprint` matches directly and **no later run with any agent, model, effort or command will ever re-derive those facts**.

That is reachable in exactly the situation the PR describes: the setup backfill runs `--agent codex --effort low`, codex exits 0 but emits a refusal, a rate-limit body, or output in the wrong format. The only recovery is a branch-wide `--force`, which first drops every distilled fact on the branch (`--session` plus `--force` is rejected at `:992`).

Reproduced:

```
on PR HEAD:                       POISON: pass-2 chunk calls=0 facts=0   -> FAIL (facts lost)
with the old agent-bearing salt:  POISON: pass-2 chunk calls=1 facts=1   -> PASS
```

So this is introduced here, not inherited.

Fix that keeps the PR's intent: do not write a cache entry for a session whose every chunk returned zero records — or mark it retry-once. Re-adding agent/model to the salt would undo the whole point.

Related: `AgentCommand` (`:2499`, the joined argv of `--agent command`) is the one dropped field that is not "who produced it" — it is an arbitrary user-supplied executable, including a stub or a broken wrapper. Dropping it is what makes the above reachable. Worth saying out loud in the PR body as a declared decision.

### 2. The chunk grandfathering call site is unfailable — `distill_cmd.go:349`

Deleting `&& !distillChunkDoneUnderLegacySalt(...)` at the call site leaves **all 63 distill tests green**. `TestDistillChunkDoneUnderLegacySalt` asserts the helper at `:639` directly and never drives the loop that consumes it.

That is the exact shape that shipped a bug here before: helper asserted, call site free to ignore it. The behaviour itself is correct — an end-to-end probe shows `second run dispatched 1 chunks` versus 3 without the clause, and goes red when the clause is removed. It just needs that probe (or equivalent) as a real guard.

---

### Worth fixing, not blocking

- **`grandfatheredAgentSaltFingerprint` re-hashes the full transcript per candidate salt** (`:2414`). Measured on a 4 MB transcript: 48.39ms versus 3.61ms for the content form, **13.4x per cache miss**. Salt counts: 8 for the hook, 16 for a model-pinned backfill, 36 for `--agent command` with a pinned model and effort. One-line fix: hoist `sha256.Sum256([]byte(content))` out of the loop.
- **The chunk record is migrated by reference, not rewritten** (`:1411`). On the cached path the session fingerprint is rewritten under the new salt but `carryDistillChunks` copies the chunk hashes verbatim, so that record stays legacy-salted forever and becomes dead weight the moment `distillPreprocessingVersion` bumps.
- **Enumeration gap** (`:2523`): agents are `{own, codex, claude-code}`, efforts `{"", own, "low"}`, models `{"", own}`. `ollama` is a documented first-class agent (`--agent` help at `:765`, probed at `refresh.go:863`) and is not enumerated, nor is any other effort or model. Entries those producers wrote re-pay the agent — safe direction, but the "nobody has to repeat the writer's flags" claim holds only for codex and claude-code across `{"", low}` and `{"", current model}`.
- **Dead production code**: `distillCacheSaltForBrain` (`:2361`) and `legacyAgentDistillCacheSaltsForBrain` (`:2559`) have no production callers left — the dry-run path moved to `distillSaltInputsForBrain`. They are kept alive by the new test file, so `unused` will not flag them.
- **Stale comment** at `:831`: "Resolve the agent BEFORE the dry-run branch: the cache salt hashes the agent name". It no longer does. The resolution is still needed for the own-config legacy salt and the report's `Agent` field, so keep the code and fix the comment.

Two other guards are green under weakening but harmlessly so: the `previous == ""` check at `:2415` is defensive only (an empty string can never equal a `sha256:`-prefixed fingerprint), and the branch component of the checkpoint identity fingerprint at `:2378` is redundant with the key — that line is pre-existing, only re-touched here.

### Attacks that did not reproduce

A false positive from the enumeration (every candidate binds SessionID + LatestCheckpoint + SessionIndex + branch + transcriptMode, so a match proves identity — only a SHA-256 collision would do it); the rewrite clobbering another session's entry (`url.PathEscape` on every segment makes a two-segment key uncollidable with a three-segment one); any form of cross-branch reuse, at either the session or the chunk level; the duplicate-session-id guard being bypassed; fact mutation on the checkpoint fast path or the content migration; a preprocessing-version bump matching old entries; a dry-run/run disagreement on the derived salts.

All of Suhaan's review on [entireio/entire-brain#440](https://github.com/entireio/entire-brain/pull/440) is addressed and pushed as f7420ba1. The full `internal/cli` package passes, and the PR body now documents each change. CI is running on the new head.

**The two blocking items**

- **Zero-record stickiness.** I went with retry-once rather than never-cache. A session whose every dispatched chunk returns nothing is written with an `empty:` prefix on its fingerprint. Nothing matches it, so the dry run and `status` treat the session as not distilled, the next run re-derives it once under whatever agent it has, and only a second empty result is accepted as final. Never-cache was the wrong trade: genuinely trivial sessions would re-spend on every hook run forever. The tentative entry keeps only chunk hashes the cache had already seen succeed, so the retry re-sends the empty chunks. Suhaan's POISON reproduction is now a test that runs pass 1 with an empty agent, pass 2 with a different producer landing the fact, and pass 3 cached.
- **Unfailable chunk call site.** New end-to-end test: a transcript an old agent-salted binary distilled in two chunks grows by one, and the hook's run must make exactly one agent call. I mutation-checked it: deleting the legacy clause gives three calls and the test goes red. The same check was done for the retry-once write and the chunk-record rewrite; each weakening fails exactly its test.

**The non-blocking items** are all in: content hashed once per cache miss instead of per candidate salt, the chunk record re-hashed under the new salt when a session entry is grandfathered (the checkpoint fast path has no content and self-heals on the next content change), ollama in the producer enumeration with a comment stating what is deliberately not guessed, both dead helpers removed, the stale comment fixed, and the `AgentCommand` decision declared in the PR body.

**Two things worth knowing**

- The fix exposed a live instance of the poison case in the existing suite. The fake agent in distill_order_test.go emitted `conventions.testing`, a path the taxonomy rejects, so every session in those tests was an all-empty extraction that the old code happily cached as distilled. It now emits a valid per-session path.
- When I checked out the PR branch, an uncommitted merge of origin/main appeared in the index a minute later. I did not start it, and I suspect the app's base-branch sync did. It had no conflicts and all tests ran on top of it, so I committed it as its own merge commit (bf1388e7) ahead of the fix.
